Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

vile adjective

of a person: morally filthy

also filthy (of a person), foul, low, dirty (morally), scum, you filthy creature

classical

Plaut. Bacch. 884: Quid nunc, impūre?
Cic. Cat. 2.23: omnēs adulterī, omnēs impūrī impudīcīque (Lewis & Short)

impūrus, impūra, impūrum

declension

unclean in a moral sense: filthy, vile, abandoned

Its literal sense, unclean, is very rare (Lewis & Short). The vocative impūre and the superlative impūrissime are stock abuse in comedy.

Examples

  • Quid nunc, impūre? numquid dēbētur tibi?

    Well now, you filthy creature? Are you owed anything?Plaut. Bacch. 884

  • Ō hominem impūrum!

    What a vile man!Ter. Ad. 183

See also rascal, dirty, immodest, evil.

SourcesLewis & Short: impurus

Plautus, Bacchides 884. Terence, Adelphoe 183.
